[[File:Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani - Flickr - Kevin Thiele.jpg|right|thumb|''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani'']]
'''''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Cyperaceae|sedge family]] known by the common names '''grey club-rush''',<ref name="PlantAtlas">{{cite web | title=Grey Club-rush ''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani'' (C.C.Gmel.) Palla | website=PlantAtlas | url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.m35 | access-date=2025-09-18}}</ref><ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''softstem bulrush''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SCTA2|taxon=Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani|accessdate=1 February 2016}}</ref> and '''great bulrush'''. 

== Distribution ==
It has a [[cosmopolitan distribution]], occurring in every country in Europe except for Iceland, all of temperate Asia except for Mongolia, every state in the United States (including Hawaii), every province and territory in Canada except [[Nunavut]], and in most of [[Australasia]]; only in Africa and South America is it less widespread, though still present in several countries in each.<ref name="POWO" /> It grows in wet habitats, usually in shallow water; it is most abundant in brackish and tidal [[Estuary|estuarine]] water, but also occurs widely in fresh water.<ref name="PlantAtlas" /><ref name="Streeter">{{cite book | last=Streeter | first=David | title=Flower Guide | publisher=Collins | date=2010 | isbn=978-0-00-718389-0 | page=554}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani'' is quite variable in appearance, thus explaining the long list of synonyms that have been created over the years. It is a perennial herb producing dense stands of many narrow erect stems reaching {{cvt|1|–|1.5|m|ft|0}},<ref name="Streeter"/> rarely to {{cvt|3|m|ft|0}},<ref name="FOC">{{cite web | title=''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani'' in Flora of China @ efloras.org | website=eFloras.org Home | url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242357954 | access-date=2025-11-13}}</ref> in height. It grows from a long [[rhizome]] system. The leaves are mostly basal, usually underwater, and have wide sheaths around the stems. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[panicle]] of spikelets on thin stems 2–6 cm long which spread, arch, or droop. The spikelets variably brown. There is usually a long, stiff [[bract]] alongside each spikelet or cluster of spikelets. Flowering is in early to mid summer (June to July in Britain), and fruiting in late summer to early autumn (August to September in Britain).<ref name="Streeter"/>

It is closely related to ''[[Schoenoplectus lacustris]]'' (common club-rush), being distinguished from it by its smaller size (up to 1.5 m, as opposed to 3 m), slenderer, glaucous stems, and in the flowers having just two, rather than three, [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]]s.<ref name="Streeter"/> Both share stems circular in cross-section, unlike the triangular stems of ''[[Schoenoplectus triqueter]]'' (triangular club-rush).<ref name="Streeter"/>

==Uses==
The new shoots and young roots may be eaten raw or cooked. The older roots can be made into flour.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Elias|first1=Thomas S.|title=Edible Wild Plants: A North American Field Guide to Over 200 Natural Foods|last2=Dykeman|first2=Peter A.|publisher=[[Sterling Publishing|Sterling]]|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4027-6715-9|location=New York|pages=70|oclc=244766414|orig-year=1982}}</ref>

In Hawaii, where it is known as ''‘aka‘akai'', ''kaluhā'', or ''nānaku'', its stems are made into floor mats.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://data.bishopmuseum.org/ethnobotanydb/ethnobotany.php?b=d&ID=akaakai|title= 'aka'akai|website=Hawaiian Ethnobotany Online Database|publisher=[[Bishop Museum]]|date=2023}}</ref> In New Zealand, known as ''kāpūngāwhā'', it is a source of weaving fabric.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rauropiwhakaoranga.landcareresearch.co.nz/names/b39b557c-adfd-4cf5-95db-70d1318ec46d|title=''Schoenoplectus tabernaemontani''. Kāpūngāwhā. Wāwā.|website=Ngā Rauropi Whakaoranga|publisher=Manaaki Whenua|date=2023}}</ref>

A [[cultivar]] with bright horizontal white or yellowish stripes, ''S. tabernaemontani'' 'Zebrinus', is sold as an [[ornamental plant]] for water gardens and landscaping.<ref>[http://www.europeanwatergardener.com/print_page.asp?category=354&ID=829 European Water Gardener]</ref><ref>[http://au.water-gardener.com/content.asp?Category=356 Australian Water Gardener]</ref> Solid white and yellow cultivars are also available.<ref>Darke, Rick. [https://books.google.com/books?id=CfHbOwKmetMC&dq=Schoenoplectus+tabernaemontani+zebrinus&pg=PA277 The Color Encyclopedia of Ornamental Grasses.] Timber Press. 1999. pg 277.</ref>
